signals.topic: Home yoga mat ritual in morning light
signals.summary: A quiet, environment-led home yoga practice — mat, blocks, plants and low morning light — carrying the whole 'yoga as calm' feeling without a body ever being the subject. The interest is in the space and the ritual, not the pose.
signals.why_now: r/yoga is the freshest cluster in the set: 'I'm diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder... yoga changed that' (1.1h), 'Could someone tell me more about emotions during yoga?' (14.4h), 'Shop Yoga, Pose Suggestions' (13.7h), 'Yoga like Leslie Fightmaster?' (19.7h), 'Good poses for cervical kyphosis' (24.2h) — 5 posts inside 24h. This is reinforced across-source by Yoga With Adriene evergreen flows: 'Start the Day Grounded | Morning Yoga', 'Yoga For Tight Hamstrings & Lower Back' (120h). The demand is for a calm morning practice space, which is squarely producible as an empty sunlit mat/studio.

signals.summary: A cozy sleep-sanctuary mood — dim bedroom, layered sheets, a warm lamp, legs-up-the-wall by the bed — framing sleep as a designed evening ritual. Producible entirely as a still bedroom interior, no sleeper needed, and fits the late-summer-into-autumn cocooning mood.
signals.why_now: Object/environment-led sleep interest surfaces across sources even after the medical/support noise is discarded: 'We Asked 4 Doctors Which Bed Sheets Help You Sleep Better' (79h, a bedroom-object piece), plus evergreen Yoga With Adriene wind-down flows 'Legs Up The Wall for Better Sleep' (624h) and 'Sleep Better Tonight | 10-Minute Bedtime Flow' (1296h). Sits on top of enormous but non-producible r/sleep chatter (23 threads), confirming the appetite; the producible expression is the calm bedroom itself.

signals.summary: Hyrox — the sled/wall-ball/rower functional-fitness race — is a sustained, still-accelerating mainstream trend. Producibility is limited (the obvious imagery is bodies competing), but the equipment itself — sleds, sandbags, wall balls, rowers staged in an arena — is the only producible route and keeps it below the environment-led waves.
signals.why_now: Broadest cross-source news cluster in the set: 'What to know about the Hyrox fitness trend' from Good Morning America (72h) AND ABC News (72.4h) within the same window, plus 'Inside NYC's obsession with HYROX' (nypost, 583h) and 'Is Hyrox the new CrossFit?' (USA Today, 3055h) — a wave spanning months and multiple independent outlets, still fed fresh this week. Kept as an ongoing trend, but scored down hard on producibility per the body-subject bar.

signals.summary: The 'recovery' side of wellness expressed as environments and objects — a wood-lined sauna, infrared glow, steam, cold plunge — rather than a body. Very high producibility (pure interior/object still life), held back only by a thin and older evidence base.
signals.why_now: A modest but genuine cross-source thread on recovery-as-ritual: 'Six things to know about infrared workouts' (The Conversation, 415h) and 'Biohacks or basics? What actually works in exercise recovery' (Medical Xpress, 3079h), echoed by evergreen equipment interest like 'The 5 Best Outdoor Saunas for Getting Your Sweat On' (older affiliate RSS, excluded from scoring). Weak on velocity, but the sauna/heat interior is one of the most photogenic and body-free scenes in the whole category.

signals.summary: The 'mobility / do-less' movement lane — floor stretching, foam roller, resistance band, an unrolled mat — framed as a calm daily maintenance ritual. Partially producible through the objects and floor space rather than the mover.
signals.why_now: A steady multi-source thread on approachable mobility: 'Dr Amir Khan's 3 mobility exercises to reduce stiffness' (Woman & Home, 147.6h), 'Is Yoga Enough for Building Strength and Flexibility?' (Health.com, 295h), and 'how to start a mobility practice' (The Guardian, 1303h), alongside fresh r/flexibility activity. Overlaps the intuitive/'case for doing less' trend (ELLE, 2095h). Body-adjacent, so producibility is capped, but the mat-and-props still life carries it.
